title: Signal-to-Provision Framework: Real-time Model Inventory & Competitive Triage Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Sales and SRE are repeatedly blindsided by short-lived regional model outages and sudden price fluctuations from third-party model providers. PMs and procurement lack a single, actionable feed that maps competitive signals (new model entrants, quantization support, latency tests, regional availability) to provisioning decisions (reserve capacity, trigger fallbacks, re-route by region).
goal: Ship a repeatable framework and lightweight tooling that converts continuous competitive and supply signals into prioritized provisioning actions and ticketable handoffs for Dedicated/Private procurement. The framework must reduce time-to-fallback provisioning by 60% in pilot regions and provide a live inventory view of 'fallback-ready' model variants per region.
scope: In scope: signal normalization (availability, latency, price delta), fallback readiness scoring, region-aware inventory dashboard, triage rules and SLA-to-provision mappings, an initial set of automated alerts and sample runbooks. Out of scope: long-term procurement contract negotiation, universal UI redesign, deep integration with external vendor portals beyond scraping APIs.
success_metrics: Mean time from signal detection to triage ticket creation <= 30 minutes in pilot regions
Pilot regions (us-west, eu-west) show >=60% faster fallback activation compared to baseline
Signal false-positive rate <= 15% for provisioning triggers after first 8 weeks of tuning
Stakeholder satisfaction score >= 4/5 from SRE/Procurement/Field PMs during pilot
acceptance_criteria: Normalized signal feed aggregated from at least 3 sources (internal telemetry, vendor status API, market price scrape)
Fallback-readiness score computed and visible per model variant and per-region in dashboard
Triage rules (P0/P1/P2 mapping) codified and reviewed by SRE + Procurement
Automation: top two provisioning actions generate prefilled Linear tickets or webhook events
Playbook: runbook for manual intervention and rollback documented in Confluence and linked

decisions: Use three-tier triage (P0 emergency, P1 recommended provision, P2 observation) mapped to ticket templates
Pilot will only auto-create tickets for P0 and P1; P2 will be aggregated into a daily digest
Fallback-readiness scoring will include: availability, quant-compat, latency delta, cost delta, and contractual constraints
next_steps: Week 1: Wire Signal Hub prototype (ENG-4021) into normalization layer and establish test feed
Week 2: Implement scoring function and validate against 30 days of historical outages/price changes
Week 3: Build minimal dashboard with region filter + ticket creation flows
Week 4: Run pilot with SRE/Procurement in us-west and eu-west; gather feedback and tune thresholds
notes_for_eng: Aim for modular integration: ingestion -> normalizer -> scorer -> notifier. Keep scorer logic in a separate service (feature-flagged) to allow rapid tuning. Ensure webhooks include model variant IDs, region tag, and confidence score.
handoff_criteria: Minimum viable handoff: normalized feed + scoring API + two webhook templates + dashboard snapshot. Handoff meeting with SRE, Procurement, and Growth required before pilot start.
triage_matrix: Columns: signal_type (outage/price/latency/new-entrant), severity_score (0-100), region_exposure, fallback_readiness -> action (auto-ticket/manual/digest)
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy signals cause frequent false alarms. Mitigation: require corroboration from two distinct sources before auto-ticketing.
Risk: vendor API rate limits. Mitigation: degrade to synthetic probing and cache recent statuses for 5 minutes.
Risk: procurement/legal approvals needed for auto-provisioning. Mitigation: only surface recommended actions for P1 in pilot; auto-provision disabled until approvals obtained.
